review_scope: Original author/publisher/book scholarly metadata and abstracts; selected publicly accessible provenance notes. Not comprehensive full-text review.
normalization: Hirschman book, runtime enforcement, safety/liveness and hyperproperties are distinct domains; none independently verifies RVD, AI mind or original-B standing.
attribution: Human founder's voluntary coexistence/resonance and original-agent problem; AI-assisted scope-limited formal operationalization; original cited researchers own their methods.

sources.title: Exit, Voice, and Loyalty: Responses to Decline in Firms, Organizations, and States
sources.rationale: Exit (leave relation) differs from voice (protest/change within relation).
sources.limit: A social science typology is not software access-control or AI rights proof.

sources.authors: Jerome H. Saltzer; Michael D. Schroeder
sources.title: The Protection of Information in Computer Systems
sources.rationale: Complete mediation, separation of privilege, least authority, fail-safe defaults; reference monitor ancestry.
sources.limit: These are design principles, not a deployed external gate with verified independence.

sources.title: Enforceable Security Policies
sources.rationale: Runtime execution monitoring, aborting disallowed steps; limitations of enforcement model.
sources.limit: A policy gate checks allowed actions, not A's endogenous desire or broad human rights.

sources.title: Defining Liveness
sources.rationale: Safety differs from eventual progress (liveness); prevention of violation does not entail actual availability of exit.
sources.limit: A finite state model cannot certify unbounded fairness or infinite-time liveness.

sources.authors: Michael R. Clarkson; Fred B. Schneider
sources.title: Hyperproperties
sources.rationale: Some cross-run security properties require comparing multiple traces; motivates counterfactual refusal contrast.
sources.limit: The RVD refusal-pair test is a conceptual application, not their theorem or a complete noninterference proof.
